title: Unified latency decomposition dashboard: component-level and IO-mode splits
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement: PMs and SREs need a single operational view that decomposes end-to-end request latency by serving component (gateway, router, runtime, KV cache, network) and by IO mode (streaming vs non-streaming). Current dashboards show percentiles at route/model granularity but lack span-level attribution and an easy way to compare streaming vs sync workloads side-by-side. This ticket implements a unified dashboard and the tracing/metric pipelines needed for accurate percentile decomposition and drift detection across modes.

Goals: 
- Create dashboard panels for p50/p95/p99 with waterfall-like attributions per model-route showing percentiles contributed by each component.
- Add side-by-side breakdowns for streaming vs non-streaming (same time range/filters) and an interactive toggle to switch between absolute and relative contribution.
- Surface slow-path triggers (KV cache misses, model-variant fallbacks, cross-region hops) and annotate traces.
- Add automated daily drift report (percentile delta by component + IO mode) and an alert if p95 for any component increases >20% vs 7d baseline.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- We will compute percentile attributions using weighted-percentile decomposition from span durations linked to trace IDs rather than naive subtraction of medians. This is more accurate for tail behavior but requires us to sample traces at higher rate for tail windows (see pipeline below).
- To avoid explosion of metrics cardinality we will keep the primary metric tags to {route, model, io_mode, region, release} and push span-level component breakdowns into a compressed histogram metric with a fixed bucket scheme. This trades off some granularity for long-term query performance.
- For streaming traces we will attribute streaming latency to two phases: initial response (first byte) and steady-state per-token latency. Both must be shown; steady-state will be normalized to per-token latency to allow fair comparison with sync requests.

Telemetry & pipeline changes required: 
- Tracing hooks: add a lightweight span at the router level that records io_mode and model_version; ensure runtime emits per-span "component" tag (gateway|router|runtime|kv-cache|network) and a numeric "component_latency_ms".
- Metrics pipeline: create a new histogram metric redwood.latency_components with labels {route, model, io_mode, component, region, release}. This will be derived from spans and aggregated in the metrics pipeline (Datadog/Prometheus -> metric-ingest).
- Logging: include a tracing.trace_id field in access logs for quick correlation. Add a log marker when KV cache miss occurs: kv_cache:miss=true with duration_ms.
- Sampling: increase trace sampling to 5% globally and 25% for requests with latency > p95 (adaptive tail sampling) to ensure enough tail traces for decomposition.

Dashboard implementation notes: 
- Panels: single-route view with stacked bar decomposition at p50/p95/p99, comparison view showing streaming and non-streaming columns for the same percentiles, sparkline row for 7d trend per component, and a small table of top 10 trace examples (links to trace viewer).
- Queries: percentile(histogram) over redwood.latency_components grouped by component and io_mode. For streaming steady-state, compute per-token median from redwood.streaming_token_latency histogram.
- Annotations: show deploys (release tag) and capacity events (dedicated pool scaling) on the time series.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Dashboard exists in Console Observability under "Model route latency decomposition" and supports filters for route, model, io_mode, region, and time range.
- Percentile decomposition for p50/p95/p99 matches sampled-trace waterfall on at least 95% of tested routes (validation plan below).
- Drift detection job runs daily and fires an alert channel (#observability-alerts) when p95 component delta >20% vs 7d baseline.

Validation plan: 
- Synthetic tests: run a traffic replay with injected latencies per component and verify dashboard decomposition recovers injected values within 10% error.
- Production spot-check: compare dashboard attribution with manual span waterfall for 50 sampled traces across 10 routes; require >=95% agreement on dominant component for p95 events.

Dependencies: 
- Tracing hooks change (runtime and router instrumentations) — sync with ENG-47290 (runtime-instrumentation) and ENG-48410 (router-tracing).
- Metrics pipeline ETL capacity — coordinate with infra team (ENG-49822).

Rollout plan: 
- Phase 1 (staging): enable enhanced spans and histogram pipeline for staging only, build dashboard with synthetic data (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (canary): enable sampling and metrics in a single region for low-traffic orgs, run 24h validation (1 week).
- Phase 3 (GA): enable for all hosted routes, enable daily drift job and alerts, and publish runbook (2 weeks).

Operational runbook pointers: provide quick actions for incidents: how to toggle sampling back down, how to disable histogram ingestion for a model-route, how to correlate traces to request IDs. Will be added to Confluence after Phase 1.

Streaming steady-state normalized to per-token latency and displayed alongside initial-response metrics
Daily drift job detects percentiles deltas and sends alerts to #observability-alerts
Validation with synthetic traffic demonstrates <=10% error on attribution
